question: Can you calculate the 5-day symmetric moving average of predicted toy sales for December 5 to 8, 2018, using daily sales data from January 1, 2017, to August 29, 2018, with a simple linear regression model? Finally provide the sum of those four 5-day moving averages?
generated_sql:
WITH daily_sales AS (
  SELECT date(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS sale_date,
         sum(oi.price) AS daily_sales
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  JOIN product_category_name_translation pcnt ON p.product_category_name = pcnt.product_category_name
  WHERE date(o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2018-08-29'
    AND lower(pcnt.product_category_name_english) = 'toys'
  GROUP BY sale_date
),
reg_params AS (
  SELECT
    (cnt * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (cnt * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x) AS slope,
    (sum_y - ((cnt * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (cnt * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x)) * sum_x) / cnt AS intercept
  FROM (
    SELECT
      count(*) AS cnt,
      sum(julianday(sale_date)) AS sum_x,
      sum(daily_sales) AS sum_y,
      sum(julianday(sale_date) * daily_sales) AS sum_xy,
      sum(julianday(sale_date) * julianday(sale_date)) AS sum_x2
    FROM daily_sales
  )
),
pred_dates AS (
  SELECT date('2018-12-03', '+' || (lvl-1) || ' days') AS pred_date
  FROM (
    SELECT 1 AS lvl UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8
  )
),
predictions AS (
  SELECT pd.pred_date,
         rp.slope * julianday(pd.pred_date) + rp.intercept AS predicted_sales
  FROM pred_dates pd
  CROSS JOIN reg_params rp
),
moving_avg AS (
  SELECT pred_date,
         AVG(predicted_sales) OVER (ORDER BY pred_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING) AS ma5
  FROM predictions
)
SELECT SUM(ma5) AS total_ma5_sum
FROM moving_avg
WHERE pred_date BETWEEN '2018-12-05' AND '2018-12-08';

question: According to the RFM definition document, calculate the average sales per order for each customer within distinct RFM segments, considering only 'delivered' orders. Use the customer unique identifier. Clearly define how to calculate Recency based on the latest purchase timestamp and specify the criteria for classifying RFM segments. The average sales should be computed as the total spend divided by the total number of orders. Please analyze and report the differences in average sales across the RFM segments
generated_sql:
WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
),
order_totals AS (
    SELECT oi.order_id,
           SUM(oi.price + oi.freight_value) AS order_total
    FROM order_items oi
    GROUP BY oi.order_id
),
customer_agg AS (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
           COUNT(do.order_id) AS order_count,
           SUM(ot.order_total) AS total_sales,
           MAX(do.order_purchase_timestamp) AS latest_purchase
    FROM customers c
    JOIN delivered_orders do ON c.customer_id = do.customer_id
    JOIN order_totals ot ON do.order_id = ot.order_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
customer_rfm AS (
    SELECT *,
           CAST(julianday('now') - julianday(latest_purchase) AS INTEGER) AS recency_days,
           total_sales / order_count AS avg_sales_per_order,
           CASE
               WHEN CAST(julianday('now') - julianday(latest_purchase) AS INTEGER) <= 30 THEN 'R1'
               WHEN CAST(julianday('now') - julianday(latest_purchase) AS INTEGER) <= 60 THEN 'R2'
               ELSE 'R3'
           END AS recency_score,
           CASE
               WHEN order_count >= 10 THEN 'F1'
               WHEN order_count >= 5 THEN 'F2'
               ELSE 'F3'
           END AS frequency_score,
           CASE
               WHEN total_sales >= 1000 THEN 'M1'
               WHEN total_sales >= 500 THEN 'M2'
               ELSE 'M3'
           END AS monetary_score
    FROM customer_agg
),
customer_segments AS (
    SELECT customer_unique_id,
           avg_sales_per_order,
           recency_score || frequency_score || monetary_score AS rfm_segment
    FROM customer_rfm
)
SELECT rfm_segment,
       AVG(avg_sales_per_order) AS avg_sales_per_order_by_segment,
       COUNT(*) AS customers_in_segment
FROM customer_segments
GROUP BY rfm_segment
ORDER BY rfm_segment;
gold_sql:
WITH RecencyScore AS (
    SELECT customer_unique_id,
           MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_purchase,
           NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) DESC) AS recency
    FROM orders
        JOIN customers USING (customer_id)
    WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY customer_unique_id
),
FrequencyScore AS (
    SELECT customer_unique_id,
           COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders,
           NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(order_id) DESC) AS frequency
    FROM orders
        JOIN customers USING (customer_id)
    WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY customer_unique_id
),
MonetaryScore AS (
    SELECT customer_unique_id,
           SUM(price) AS total_spent,
           NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY SUM(price) DESC) AS monetary
    FROM orders
        JOIN order_items USING (order_id)
        JOIN customers USING (customer_id)
    WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY customer_unique_id
),

-- 2. Assign each customer to a group
RFM AS (
    SELECT last_purchase, total_orders, total_spent,
        CASE
            WHEN recency = 1 AND frequency + monetary IN (1, 2, 3, 4) THEN "Champions"
            WHEN recency IN (4, 5) AND frequency + monetary IN (1, 2) THEN "Can't Lose Them"
            WHEN recency IN (4, 5) AND frequency + monetary IN (3, 4, 5, 6) THEN "Hibernating"
            WHEN recency IN (4, 5) AND frequency + monetary IN (7, 8, 9, 10) THEN "Lost"
            WHEN recency IN (2, 3) AND frequency + monetary IN (1, 2, 3, 4) THEN "Loyal Customers"
            WHEN recency = 3 AND frequency + monetary IN (5, 6) THEN "Needs Attention"
            WHEN recency = 1 AND frequency + monetary IN (7, 8) THEN "Recent Users"
            WHEN recency = 1 AND frequency + monetary IN (5, 6) OR
                recency = 2 AND frequency + monetary IN (5, 6, 7, 8) THEN "Potentital Loyalists"
            WHEN recency = 1 AND frequency + monetary IN (9, 10) THEN "Price Sensitive"
            WHEN recency = 2 AND frequency + monetary IN (9, 10) THEN "Promising"
            WHEN recency = 3 AND frequency + monetary IN (7, 8, 9, 10) THEN "About to Sleep"
        END AS RFM_Bucket
    FROM RecencyScore
        JOIN FrequencyScore USING (customer_unique_id)
        JOIN MonetaryScore USING (customer_unique_id)
)

SELECT RFM_Bucket, 
       AVG(total_spent / total_orders) AS avg_sales_per_customer
FROM RFM
GROUP BY RFM_Bucket

question: Could you tell me the number of orders, average payment per order and customer lifespan in weeks of the 3 custumers with the highest average payment per order, where the lifespan is calculated by subtracting the earliest purchase date from the latest purchase date in days, dividing by seven, and if the result is less than seven days, setting it to 1.0?
generated_sql:
WITH cust_stats AS (
    SELECT
        o.customer_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count,
        CAST(SUM(p.payment_value) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS avg_payment,
        CASE
            WHEN ((julianday(MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp)) - julianday(MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp))) / 7) < 1
            THEN 1.0
            ELSE ((julianday(MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp)) - julianday(MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp))) / 7)
        END AS lifespan_weeks
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id
    GROUP BY o.customer_id
)
SELECT
    customer_id,
    order_count,
    avg_payment,
    lifespan_weeks
FROM cust_stats
ORDER BY avg_payment DESC
LIMIT 3;
gold_sql:
WITH CustomerData AS (
    SELECT
        customer_unique_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT orders.order_id) AS order_count,
        SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment,
        JULIANDAY(MIN(order_purchase_timestamp)) AS first_order_day,
        JULIANDAY(MAX(order_purchase_timestamp)) AS last_order_day
    FROM customers
        JOIN orders USING (customer_id)
        JOIN order_payments USING (order_id)
    GROUP BY customer_unique_id
)
SELECT
    customer_unique_id,
    order_count AS PF,
    ROUND(total_payment / order_count, 2) AS AOV,
    CASE
        WHEN (last_order_day - first_order_day) < 7 THEN
            1
        ELSE
            (last_order_day - first_order_day) / 7
        END AS ACL
FROM CustomerData
ORDER BY AOV DESC
LIMIT 3

question: Could you help me calculate the average single career span value in years for all baseball players? Please precise the result as a float number. First, calculate the difference in years, months, and days between the debut and final game dates. For each player, the career span is computed as the sum of the absolute number of years, plus the absolute number of months divided by 12, plus the absolute number of days divided by 365. Round each part to two decimal places before summing. Finally, average the career spans and round the result to a float number.
generated_sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(career_span), 2) AS avg_career_span
FROM (
  SELECT 
    ROUND(years, 2) + ROUND(months, 2) / 12.0 + ROUND(days, 2) / 365.0 AS career_span
  FROM (
    SELECT 
      ABS(CAST(strftime('%Y', final_game) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', debut) AS INTEGER)) AS years,
      ABS(CAST(strftime('%m', final_game) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%m', debut) AS INTEGER)) AS months,
      ABS(CAST(strftime('%d', final_game) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%d', debut) AS INTEGER)) AS days
    FROM player
    WHERE debut IS NOT NULL AND final_game IS NOT NULL
  )
);

         SUM(b.r) AS total_r,
         SUM(b.h) AS total_h,
         SUM(b.hr) AS total_hr

  JOIN batting b ON p.player_id = b.player_id

         MAX(total_r) AS max_r,

question: What is the distance of the longest route where Abakan is either the departure or destination city (in kilometers)?
generated_sql:
WITH route_dist AS (
    SELECT 
        6371 * 2 * atan2(
            sqrt(
                sin(((sub.lat2 - sub.lat1) * 0.017453292519943295) / 2) * sin(((sub.lat2 - sub.lat1) * 0.017453292519943295) / 2) +
                cos(sub.lat1 * 0.017453292519943295) * cos(sub.lat2 * 0.017453292519943295) *
                sin(((sub.lon2 - sub.lon1) * 0.017453292519943295) / 2) * sin(((sub.lon2 - sub.lon1) * 0.017453292519943295) / 2)
            ),
            sqrt(1 - (
                sin(((sub.lat2 - sub.lat1) * 0.017453292519943295) / 2) * sin(((sub.lat2 - sub.lat1) * 0.017453292519943295) / 2) +
                cos(sub.lat1 * 0.017453292519943295) * cos(sub.lat2 * 0.017453292519943295) *
                sin(((sub.lon2 - sub.lon1) * 0.017453292519943295) / 2) * sin(((sub.lon2 - sub.lon1) * 0.017453292519943295) / 2)
            ))
        ) AS distance_km
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            CAST(substr(d.coordinates, 1, instr(d.coordinates, ',')-1) AS REAL) AS lat1,
            CAST(substr(d.coordinates, instr(d.coordinates, ',')+1) AS REAL) AS lon1,
            CAST(substr(a.coordinates, 1, instr(a.coordinates, ',')-1) AS REAL) AS lat2,
            CAST(substr(a.coordinates, instr(a.coordinates, ',')+1) AS REAL) AS lon2
        FROM flights f
        JOIN airports_data d ON f.departure_airport = d.airport_code
        JOIN airports_data a ON f.arrival_airport = a.airport_code
        WHERE d.city = 'Abakan' OR a.city = 'Abakan'
    ) sub
)
SELECT MAX(distance_km) AS longest_distance_km FROM route_dist;

question: Distribute all the unique city pairs into the distance ranges 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, and 6000+, based on their average distance of all routes between them. Then how many pairs are there in the distance range with the fewest unique city paires?
generated_sql:
WITH airport_coords AS (
  SELECT airport_code,
         city,
         CAST(substr(coordinates, 1, instr(coordinates, ',')-1) AS REAL) AS lat,
         CAST(substr(coordinates, instr(coordinates, ',')+1) AS REAL) AS lon
  FROM airports_data
),
flight_dist AS (
  SELECT f.flight_id,
         ac1.city AS city1,
         ac2.city AS city2,
         sqrt((ac2.lat - ac1.lat)*(ac2.lat - ac1.lat) + (ac2.lon - ac1.lon)*(ac2.lon - ac1.lon)) * 111.0 AS distance
  FROM flights f
  JOIN airport_coords ac1 ON f.departure_airport = ac1.airport_code
  JOIN airport_coords ac2 ON f.arrival_airport = ac2.airport_code
),
city_pairs AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN city1 < city2 THEN city1 ELSE city2 END AS city_a,
         CASE WHEN city1 < city2 THEN city2 ELSE city1 END AS city_b,
         AVG(distance) AS avg_dist
  FROM flight_dist
  GROUP BY city_a, city_b
),
 buckets AS (
  SELECT CASE 
           WHEN avg_dist < 1000 THEN '0-999'
           WHEN avg_dist < 2000 THEN '1000-1999'
           WHEN avg_dist < 3000 THEN '2000-2999'
           WHEN avg_dist < 4000 THEN '3000-3999'
           WHEN avg_dist < 5000 THEN '4000-4999'
           WHEN avg_dist < 6000 THEN '5000-5999'
           ELSE '6000+'
         END AS bucket,
         COUNT(*) AS pair_count
  FROM city_pairs
  GROUP BY bucket
)
SELECT pair_count
FROM buckets
ORDER BY pair_count ASC
LIMIT 1;

question: Please calculate the fatality rate for motorcycle collisions, separated by helmet usage. Specifically, calculate two percentages: 1) the percentage of motorcyclist fatalities in collisions where parties (drivers or passengers) were wearing helmets, and 2) the percentage of motorcyclist fatalities in collisions where parties were not wearing helmets. For each group, compute this by dividing the total number of motorcyclist fatalities by the total number of collisions involving that group. Use the parties table to determine helmet usage (from party_safety_equipment fields).
generated_sql:
WITH motorcyclist_helmets AS (
    SELECT c.case_id,
           CASE WHEN EXISTS (
               SELECT 1 FROM parties p
               WHERE p.case_id = c.case_id
                 AND p.party_type = 'Motorcyclist'
                 AND (p.party_safety_equipment_1 LIKE '%Helmet%' OR p.party_safety_equipment_2 LIKE '%Helmet%')
           ) THEN 'Worn' ELSE 'Not Worn' END AS helmet_status
    FROM collisions c
    WHERE c.motorcycle_collision = 1
)
SELECT mh.helmet_status,
       COUNT(*) AS total_collisions,
       SUM(CASE WHEN c.motorcyclist_killed_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fatal_collisions,
       CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN c.motorcyclist_killed_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) * 100.0 AS fatality_rate_percent
FROM motorcyclist_helmets mh
JOIN collisions c ON mh.case_id = c.case_id
GROUP BY mh.helmet_status;

question: For the primary collision factor violation category that was the most common cause of traffic accidents in 2021, how many percentage points did its share of annual road incidents in 2021 decrease compared to its share in 2011?
generated_sql:
WITH top_cat AS (
    SELECT LOWER(c.pcf_violation_category) AS category
    FROM collisions c
    JOIN case_ids ci ON c.case_id = ci.case_id
    WHERE ci.db_year = 2021
      AND c.pcf_violation_category IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY LOWER(c.pcf_violation_category)
    ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
    LIMIT 1
), stats AS (
    SELECT
        SUM(CASE WHEN ci.db_year = 2021 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_2021,
        SUM(CASE WHEN ci.db_year = 2011 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_2011,
        SUM(CASE WHEN ci.db_year = 2021 AND LOWER(c.pcf_violation_category) = (SELECT category FROM top_cat) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_2021,
        SUM(CASE WHEN ci.db_year = 2011 AND LOWER(c.pcf_violation_category) = (SELECT category FROM top_cat) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_2011
    FROM collisions c
    JOIN case_ids ci ON c.case_id = ci.case_id
)
SELECT ROUND(
    (CASE WHEN total_2011 > 0 THEN cnt_2011 * 100.0 / total_2011 ELSE 0 END) -
    (CASE WHEN total_2021 > 0 THEN cnt_2021 * 100.0 / total_2021 ELSE 0 END)
, 2) AS percentage_point_decrease
FROM stats;

question: For the NXT title that had the shortest match (excluding titles with "title change"), what were the names of the two wrestlers involved?
generated_sql:
SELECT w1.name AS wrestler1, w2.name AS wrestler2
FROM Matches m
JOIN Belts b ON m.title_id = b.id
JOIN Wrestlers w1 ON m.winner_id = w1.id
JOIN Wrestlers w2 ON m.loser_id = w2.id
WHERE b.name LIKE '%NXT%'
  AND m.title_change = 0
  AND m.duration = (
    SELECT MIN(m2.duration)
    FROM Matches m2
    JOIN Belts b2 ON m2.title_id = b2.id
    WHERE b2.name LIKE '%NXT%'
      AND m2.title_change = 0
  );
gold_sql:
WITH MatchDetails AS (
    SELECT
        b.name AS titles,
        m.duration AS match_duration,
        w1.name || ' vs ' || w2.name AS matches,
        m.win_type AS win_type,
        l.name AS location,
        e.name AS event,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY b.name ORDER BY m.duration ASC) AS rank
    FROM 
        Belts b
    INNER JOIN Matches m ON m.title_id = b.id
    INNER JOIN Wrestlers w1 ON w1.id = m.winner_id
    INNER JOIN Wrestlers w2 ON w2.id = m.loser_id
    INNER JOIN Cards c ON c.id = m.card_id
    INNER JOIN Locations l ON l.id = c.location_id
    INNER JOIN Events e ON e.id = c.event_id
    INNER JOIN Promotions p ON p.id = c.promotion_id
    WHERE
        p.name = 'NXT'
        AND m.duration <> ''
        AND b.name <> ''
        AND b.name NOT IN (
            SELECT name 
            FROM Belts 
            WHERE name LIKE '%title change%'
        )
),
Rank1 AS (
SELECT 
    titles,
    match_duration,
    matches,
    win_type,
    location,
    event
FROM 
    MatchDetails
WHERE 
    rank = 1
)
SELECT
    SUBSTR(matches, 1, INSTR(matches, ' vs ') - 1) AS wrestler1,
    SUBSTR(matches, INSTR(matches, ' vs ') + 4) AS wrestler2
FROM
Rank1
ORDER BY match_duration 
LIMIT 1

question: Which bowler has the lowest bowling average per wicket taken?
generated_sql:
WITH runs AS (
    SELECT b.bowler AS bowler_id,
           SUM(COALESCE(s.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored s ON b.match_id = s.match_id AND b.over_id = s.over_id AND b.ball_id = s.ball_id AND b.innings_no = s.innings_no
    LEFT JOIN extra_runs e ON b.match_id = e.match_id AND b.over_id = e.over_id AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
    GROUP BY b.bowler
),
wickets AS (
    SELECT b.bowler AS bowler_id,
           COUNT(*) AS wickets
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    JOIN wicket_taken w ON b.match_id = w.match_id AND b.over_id = w.over_id AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id AND b.innings_no = w.innings_no
    GROUP BY b.bowler
)
SELECT p.player_name,
       CAST(r.total_runs AS REAL) / w.wickets AS bowling_average
FROM runs r

ORDER BY bowling_average ASC

question: Retrieve the names of players who scored no less than 100 runs in a match while playing for the team that lost that match.
generated_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT p.player_name
FROM player p
JOIN (
    SELECT b.striker AS player_id, b.match_id, SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS total_runs
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    JOIN batsman_scored bs ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
        AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
        AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
        AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    GROUP BY b.striker, b.match_id
    HAVING SUM(bs.runs_scored) >= 100
) pr ON p.player_id = pr.player_id
JOIN player_match pm ON pm.player_id = pr.player_id AND pm.match_id = pr.match_id
JOIN match m ON m.match_id = pr.match_id
WHERE pm.team_id != m.match_winner;
gold_sql:
-- Step 1: Calculate players' total runs in each match
WITH player_runs AS (
    SELECT 
        bbb.striker AS player_id, 
        bbb.match_id, 
        SUM(bsc.runs_scored) AS total_runs 
    FROM 
        ball_by_ball AS bbb
    JOIN 
        batsman_scored AS bsc
    ON 
        bbb.match_id = bsc.match_id 
        AND bbb.over_id = bsc.over_id 
        AND bbb.ball_id = bsc.ball_id 
        AND bbb.innings_no = bsc.innings_no
    GROUP BY 
        bbb.striker, bbb.match_id
    HAVING 
        SUM(bsc.runs_scored) >= 100
),

-- Step 2: Identify losing teams for each match
losing_teams AS (
    SELECT 
        match_id, 
        CASE 
            WHEN match_winner = team_1 THEN team_2 
            ELSE team_1 
        END AS loser 
    FROM 
        match
),

-- Step 3: Combine the above results to get players who scored 100 or more runs in losing teams
players_in_losing_teams AS (
    SELECT 
        pr.player_id, 
        pr.match_id 
    FROM 
        player_runs AS pr
    JOIN 
        losing_teams AS lt
    ON 
        pr.match_id = lt.match_id
    JOIN 
        player_match AS pm
    ON 
        pr.player_id = pm.player_id 
        AND pr.match_id = pm.match_id 
        AND lt.loser = pm.team_id
)

-- Step 4: Select distinct player names from the player table
SELECT DISTINCT 
    p.player_name 
FROM 
    player AS p
JOIN 
    players_in_losing_teams AS plt
ON 
    p.player_id = plt.player_id
ORDER BY 
    p.player_name;

question: Please help me find the names of top 5 players with the highest average runs per match in season 5, along with their batting averages.
generated_sql:
WITH season_matches AS (
    SELECT match_id
    FROM match
    WHERE season_id = 5
),
player_runs AS (
    SELECT b.striker AS player_id,
           b.match_id,
           SUM(COALESCE(s.runs_scored, 0)) AS runs
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    JOIN batsman_scored s ON b.match_id = s.match_id
                         AND b.over_id = s.over_id
                         AND b.ball_id = s.ball_id
    WHERE b.match_id IN (SELECT match_id FROM season_matches)
    GROUP BY b.striker, b.match_id
),
player_match_counts AS (
    SELECT pm.player_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT pm.match_id) AS matches_played
    FROM player_match pm
    WHERE pm.match_id IN (SELECT match_id FROM season_matches)
    GROUP BY pm.player_id
),
player_dismissals AS (
    SELECT wt.player_out AS player_id,
           COUNT(*) AS dismissals
    FROM wicket_taken wt
    WHERE wt.match_id IN (SELECT match_id FROM season_matches)
    GROUP BY wt.player_out
),
player_totals AS (
    SELECT pr.player_id,
           SUM(pr.runs) AS total_runs,
           COALESCE(pmc.matches_played, 0) AS matches_played,
           COALESCE(pd.dismissals, 0) AS dismissals
    FROM player_runs pr
    LEFT JOIN player_match_counts pmc ON pr.player_id = pmc.player_id
    LEFT JOIN player_dismissals pd ON pr.player_id = pd.player_id
    GROUP BY pr.player_id
)
SELECT p.player_name,
       CAST(total_runs AS REAL) / matches_played AS avg_runs_per_match,
       CASE WHEN dismissals = 0 THEN NULL ELSE CAST(total_runs AS REAL) / dismissals END AS batting_average
FROM player_totals pt
JOIN player p ON pt.player_id = p.player_id
WHERE matches_played > 0
ORDER BY avg_runs_per_match DESC
LIMIT 5;

    SELECT 
        bb.striker AS player_id,
        bb.match_id,
        bs.runs_scored AS runs
    FROM 
        ball_by_ball AS bb
    JOIN 
        batsman_scored AS bs ON bb.match_id = bs.match_id 
            AND bb.over_id = bs.over_id 
            AND bb.ball_id = bs.ball_id 
            AND bb.innings_no = bs.innings_no
    WHERE 
        bb.match_id IN (SELECT match_id FROM match WHERE season_id = 5)
),
total_runs AS (
    SELECT 
        player_id, 
        match_id, 
        SUM(runs) AS total_runs 
    FROM 
        runs_scored 
    GROUP BY 
        player_id, match_id
),
batting_averages AS (
    SELECT 
        player_id, 
        SUM(total_runs) AS runs, 
        COUNT(match_id) AS num_matches,
        ROUND(SUM(total_runs) / CAST(COUNT(match_id) AS FLOAT), 3) AS batting_avg
    FROM 
        total_runs 
    GROUP BY 
        player_id 
    ORDER BY 
        batting_avg DESC 
    LIMIT 5
)
SELECT 
    p.player_name,
    b.batting_avg
FROM 
    player AS p
JOIN 
    batting_averages AS b ON p.player_id = b.player_id
ORDER BY

question: For each match, considering every innings, please combine runs from both batsman scored and extra runs for each over, then identify the single over with the highest total runs, retrieve the bowler for that over from the ball by ball table, and calculate the average of these highest over totals across all matches, ensuring that all runs and bowler details are accurately reflected.
generated_sql:
WITH all_runs AS (
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id, runs_scored AS runs
    FROM batsman_scored
    UNION ALL
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id, extra_runs AS runs
    FROM extra_runs
),
total_per_over AS (
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id, SUM(runs) AS total_runs
    FROM all_runs
    GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id
),
ranked_over AS (
    SELECT match_id, innings_no, over_id, total_runs,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY match_id ORDER BY total_runs DESC) AS rn
    FROM total_per_over
),
max_over AS (
    SELECT r.match_id,
           r.innings_no,
           r.over_id,
           r.total_runs,
           MIN(b.bowler) AS bowler
    FROM ranked_over r
    JOIN ball_by_ball b ON b.match_id = r.match_id
                         AND b.innings_no = r.innings_no
                         AND b.over_id = r.over_id
    WHERE r.rn = 1
    GROUP BY r.match_id, r.innings_no, r.over_id, r.total_runs
)
SELECT match_id,
       over_id,
       bowler,
       total_runs,
       (SELECT AVG(total_runs) FROM max_over) AS avg_highest_over_runs
FROM max_over;

question: Please help me identify the top 3 bowlers who, in the overs where the maximum runs were conceded in each match, gave up the highest number of runs in a single over across all matches. For each of these bowlers, provide the match in which they conceded these maximum runs. Only consider overs that had the most runs conceded within their respective matches, and among these, determine which bowlers conceded the most runs in a single over overall.
generated_sql:
WITH over_totals AS (
    SELECT b.match_id,
           b.innings_no,
           b.over_id,
           b.bowler,
           SUM(COALESCE(s.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored s
        ON b.match_id = s.match_id
        AND b.innings_no = s.innings_no
        AND b.over_id = s.over_id
        AND b.ball_id = s.ball_id
    LEFT JOIN extra_runs e
        ON b.match_id = e.match_id
        AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
        AND b.over_id = e.over_id
        AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id
    GROUP BY b.match_id, b.innings_no, b.over_id, b.bowler
),
match_max AS (
    SELECT match_id,
           MAX(total_runs) AS max_runs
    FROM over_totals
    GROUP BY match_id
),
selected_overs AS (
    SELECT ot.match_id,
           ot.innings_no,
           ot.over_id,
           ot.bowler,
           ot.total_runs
    FROM over_totals ot
    JOIN match_max mm
        ON ot.match_id = mm.match_id
        AND ot.total_runs = mm.max_runs
),
bowler_max AS (
    SELECT bowler,
           MAX(total_runs) AS max_total
    FROM selected_overs
    GROUP BY bowler

question: What is the median of the average monthly projected sales in USD for France in 2021, calculated by using the monthly sales data from 2019 and 2020 (filtered by promo_total_id=1 and channel_total_id=1), applying the growth rate from 2019 to 2020 to project 2021, converting to USD based on the currency table, and then determining the monthly averages before finding their median?
generated_sql:
WITH sales_monthly AS (
  SELECT 
    t.calendar_year,
    t.calendar_month_number AS month,
    SUM(s.amount_sold) AS total_amount
  FROM sales s
  JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
  JOIN countries cn ON c.country_id = cn.country_id
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  JOIN promotions p ON s.promo_id = p.promo_id
  JOIN channels ch ON s.channel_id = ch.channel_id
  WHERE LOWER(cn.country_name) = 'france'
    AND p.promo_total_id = 1
    AND ch.channel_total_id = 1
    AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
  GROUP BY t.calendar_year, t.calendar_month_number
),
pivot AS (
  SELECT 
    month,
    MAX(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2019 THEN total_amount END) AS sales_2019,
    MAX(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2020 THEN total_amount END) AS sales_2020
  FROM sales_monthly
  GROUP BY month
),
projected AS (
  SELECT 
    month,
    sales_2020 * (sales_2020 / NULLIF(sales_2019, 0)) AS projected_2021
  FROM pivot
),
converted AS (
  SELECT 
    p.month,
    p.projected_2021 * cu.to_us AS projected_usd
  FROM projected p
  JOIN currency cu ON LOWER(cu.country) = LOWER('France') AND cu.year = 2021 AND cu.month = p.month
)
SELECT AVG(projected_usd) AS median_projected_usd
FROM (
  SELECT projected_usd
  FROM converted
  ORDER BY projected_usd
  LIMIT 2 - (SELECT COUNT(*) % 2 FROM converted)
  OFFSET (SELECT (COUNT(*) - 1) / 2 FROM converted)
);

question: What is the average projected monthly sales in USD for France in 2021, considering only product sales with promotions where promo_total_id = 1 and channels where channel_total_id = 1, by taking each product’s monthly sales from 2019 and 2020, calculating the growth rate from 2019 to 2020 for that same product and month, applying this growth rate to project 2021 monthly sales, converting all projected 2021 amounts to USD with the 2021 exchange rates, and finally averaging and listing them by month?
generated_sql:
WITH filtered_sales AS (
  SELECT s.prod_id,
         t.calendar_year,
         t.calendar_month_number,
         s.amount_sold
  FROM sales s
  JOIN customers cu ON s.cust_id = cu.cust_id
  JOIN countries co ON cu.country_id = co.country_id
  JOIN promotions p ON s.promo_id = p.promo_id
  JOIN channels ch ON s.channel_id = ch.channel_id
  JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
  WHERE LOWER(co.country_name) = 'france'
    AND p.promo_total_id = 1
    AND ch.channel_total_id = 1
    AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
),
sales_agg AS (
  SELECT prod_id,
         calendar_year,
         calendar_month_number,
         SUM(amount_sold) AS total_amount
  FROM filtered_sales
  GROUP BY prod_id, calendar_year, calendar_month_number
),
growth AS (
  SELECT a2020.prod_id,
         a2020.calendar_month_number AS month,
         a2020.total_amount AS amount_2020,
         a2019.total_amount AS amount_2019,
         CASE WHEN a2019.total_amount = 0 THEN 0
              ELSE a2020.total_amount * 1.0 / a2019.total_amount END AS growth_rate
  FROM sales_agg a2020
  LEFT JOIN sales_agg a2019
    ON a2020.prod_id = a2019.prod_id
   AND a2020.calendar_month_number = a2019.calendar_month_number
   AND a2019.calendar_year = 2019
  WHERE a2020.calendar_year = 2020
),
projected AS (
  SELECT prod_id,
         month,
         amount_2020 * growth_rate AS projected_amount_2021
  FROM growth
),
projected_usd AS (
  SELECT p.month,
         p.projected_amount_2021 * c.to_us AS projected_usd
  FROM projected p
  JOIN currency c
    ON LOWER(c.country) = 'france'
   AND c.year = 2021
   AND c.month = p.month
)
SELECT month,
       AVG(projected_usd) AS avg_projected_sales_usd
FROM projected_usd
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;

           s.quantity_sold,
           c.unit_price,
           c.unit_cost
    FROM sales s

Additionally, calculate the year-over-year growth percentages for both the monthly total and the running total for each month, comparing each year to the previous year. WITH monthly_counts AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS month_num,

  FROM cities
  WHERE strftime('%Y', insert_date) IN ('2021','2022','2023')
    AND strftime('%m', insert_date) IN ('04','05','06')
  GROUP BY year, month_num
),
 cumulative AS (

 growth AS (

question: Identify the country with data inserted on nine different days in January 2022. Then, find the longest consecutive period with data insertions for this country during January 2022, and calculate the proportion of entries that are from its capital city within this longest consecutive insertion period.

WITH filtered AS (
    SELECT country_code_2, DATE(insert_date) AS ins_date
    FROM cities
    WHERE insert_date >= '2022-01-01' AND insert_date < '2022-02-01'

country_counts AS (

    FROM filtered

target_country AS (

),
ordered_dates AS (

           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ins_date) AS rn
    FROM country_dates
),
grouped_seq AS (
    SELECT DATE(ins_date, '-' || rn || ' day') AS grp,
           MIN(ins_date) AS start_date,

question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.

WITH months AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month
    FROM customer_transactions
),
customers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
    FROM customer_transactions
),
base AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id, m.month
    FROM customers c CROSS JOIN months m
),
monthly_txn AS (
    SELECT customer_id,
           strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month,
           SUM(txn_amount) AS net_amount
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id, month
),
combined AS (
    SELECT b.customer_id,
           b.month,
           COALESCE(t.net_amount, 0) AS net_amount
    FROM base b
    LEFT JOIN monthly_txn t
        ON b.customer_id = t.customer_id AND b.month = t.month
),
balances AS (
    SELECT customer_id,
           month,
           SUM(net_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month) AS closing_balance
    FROM combined
)
SELECT
    b.customer_id,
    b.month,
    b.closing_balance,
    b.closing_balance - COALESCE(LAG(b.closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY b.customer_id ORDER BY b.month), 0) AS monthly_change,
    b.closing_balance AS cumulative_balance
FROM balances b
ORDER BY b.customer_id, b.month;

SELECT ph.product_id,
       SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(e.event_type) = 'view' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS view_count,
       SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(e.event_type) = 'add_to_cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS add_to_cart_count,
       SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(e.event_type) = 'purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchase_count,
       (SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(e.event_type) = 'add_to_cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(e.event_type) = 'purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS left_in_cart_count
FROM shopping_cart_events e
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy ph ON e.page_id = ph.page_id
WHERE ph.page_id NOT IN (1, 2, 12, 13)
GROUP BY ph.product_id;

WITH product_viewed AS (
    SELECT
        t1.page_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN event_type = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_page_views,
        SUM(CASE WHEN event_type = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_added_to_cart
    FROM
        shopping_cart_page_hierarchy AS t1
    JOIN
        shopping_cart_events AS t2
    ON
        t1.page_id = t2.page_id
    WHERE
        t1.product_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY
        t1.page_id
),
product_purchased AS (
    SELECT
        t2.page_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN event_type = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchased_from_cart
    FROM
        shopping_cart_page_hierarchy AS t1
    JOIN
        shopping_cart_events AS t2
    ON
        t1.page_id = t2.page_id
    WHERE
        t1.product_id IS NOT NULL
        AND EXISTS (
            SELECT
                visit_id
            FROM
                shopping_cart_events
            WHERE
                event_type = 3
                AND t2.visit_id = visit_id
        )
        AND t1.page_id NOT IN (1, 2, 12, 13)
    GROUP BY
        t2.page_id
),
product_abandoned AS (
    SELECT
        t2.page_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN event_type = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abandoned_in_cart
    FROM
        shopping_cart_page_hierarchy AS t1
    JOIN
        shopping_cart_events AS t2
    ON
        t1.page_id = t2.page_id
    WHERE
        t1.product_id IS NOT NULL
        AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT
                visit_id
            FROM
                shopping_cart_events
            WHERE
                event_type = 3
                AND t2.visit_id = visit_id
        )
        AND t1.page_id NOT IN (1, 2, 12, 13)
    GROUP BY

)
SELECT
    t1.page_id,
    t1.page_name,
    t2.n_page_views AS 'number of product being viewed',
    t2.n_added_to_cart AS 'number added to the cart',
    t4.abandoned_in_cart AS 'without being purchased in cart',
    t3.purchased_from_cart AS 'count of actual purchases'
FROM
    shopping_cart_page_hierarchy AS t1
JOIN
    product_viewed AS t2 
ON
    t2.page_id = t1.page_id
JOIN
    product_purchased AS t3 
ON 
    t3.page_id = t1.page_id

ON

question: Please analyze our interest data from September 2018 to August 2019. For each month, calculate the average composition for each interest by dividing the composition by the index value. Identify the interest with the highest average composition value each month and report its average composition as the max index composition for that month. Compute the three-month rolling average of these monthly max index compositions. Ensure the output includes the date, the interest name, the max index composition for that month, the rolling average, and the names and max index compositions of the top interests from one month ago and two months ago.
generated_sql:
WITH monthly_ratios AS (
    SELECT 
        im.month_year,
        im._year,
        im._month,
        im.interest_id,
        CAST(im.composition AS REAL) / NULLIF(im.index_value, 0) AS ratio
    FROM interest_metrics im
    WHERE (im._year = 2018 AND im._month >= 9) OR (im._year = 2019 AND im._month <= 8)
),
monthly_top AS (
    SELECT 
        mr.month_year,
        mr._year,
        mr._month,
        mr.interest_id,
        COALESCE(mr.ratio, 0) AS ratio,
        im.interest_name
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            mr.*, 
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mr.month_year ORDER BY mr.ratio DESC) AS rn
        FROM monthly_ratios mr
    ) mr
    JOIN interest_map im ON im.id = mr.interest_id
    WHERE mr.rn = 1
)
SELECT 
    mt.month_year AS date,
    mt.interest_name,
    mt.ratio AS max_index_composition,
    AVG(mt.ratio) OVER (ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_average,
    COALESCE(LAG(mt.interest_name, 1) OVER (ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month), '') AS prev1_interest_name,
    COALESCE(LAG(mt.ratio, 1) OVER (ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month), 0) AS prev1_max_index_composition,
    COALESCE(LAG(mt.interest_name, 2) OVER (ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month), '') AS prev2_interest_name,
    COALESCE(LAG(mt.ratio, 2) OVER (ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month), 0) AS prev2_max_index_composition
FROM monthly_top mt
ORDER BY mt._year, mt._month;

question: For each year, calculate the percentage of films that had exclusively female actors (meaning no male actors and no actors with unknown/unspecified gender). Consider actors with gender marked as 'Male' or 'None' as non-female. For the results, display the year, the total number of movies in that year, and the percentage of movies with exclusively female actors. Extract the year from the Movie.year field by taking the last 4 characters and converting to a number.
generated_sql:
SELECT year_num AS year,
       COUNT(*) AS total_movies,
       CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN exclusive_female = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) * 100 AS percent_exclusive_female
FROM (
    SELECT m.MID,
           CAST(substr(m.year, -4) AS INTEGER) AS year_num,
           CASE WHEN EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1 FROM M_Cast mc
                    JOIN Person p ON mc.PID = p.PID
                    WHERE mc.MID = m.MID AND LOWER(p.Gender) = 'female'
                )
                AND NOT EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1 FROM M_Cast mc2
                    JOIN Person p2 ON mc2.PID = p2.PID
                    WHERE mc2.MID = m.MID AND LOWER(p2.Gender) != 'female'
                )
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS exclusive_female
    FROM Movie m
) sub
GROUP BY year_num
ORDER BY year_num

question: I need you to look into the actor collaborations and tell me how many actors have made more films with Yash Chopra than with any other director. This will help us understand his influence on the industry better.
generated_sql:
WITH y_counts AS (
    SELECT c.PID AS actor_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.MID) AS yash_cnt
    FROM M_Cast c
    JOIN M_Director d ON c.MID = d.MID
    JOIN Person pdir ON d.PID = pdir.PID
    WHERE LOWER(pdir.Name) = 'yash chopra'
    GROUP BY c.PID
), other_counts AS (
    SELECT c.PID AS actor_id, d.PID AS director_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.MID) AS cnt
    FROM M_Cast c
    JOIN M_Director d ON c.MID = d.MID
    JOIN Person pdir ON d.PID = pdir.PID
    WHERE LOWER(pdir.Name) != 'yash chopra'
    GROUP BY c.PID, d.PID
), other_max AS (
    SELECT actor_id, MAX(cnt) AS max_cnt
    FROM other_counts
    GROUP BY actor_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS actor_count
FROM y_counts yc
LEFT JOIN other_max om ON yc.actor_id = om.actor_id
WHERE yc.yash_cnt > COALESCE(om.max_cnt, 0);
gold_sql:
WITH YASH_CHOPRAS_PID AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(P.PID) AS PID
    FROM
        Person P
    WHERE
        TRIM(P.Name) = 'Yash Chopra'
),
NUM_OF_MOV_BY_ACTOR_DIRECTOR AS (
    SELECT
        TRIM(MC.PID) AS ACTOR_PID,
        TRIM(MD.PID) AS DIRECTOR_PID,
        COUNT(DISTINCT TRIM(MD.MID)) AS NUM_OF_MOV
    FROM
        M_Cast MC
    JOIN
        M_Director MD ON TRIM(MC.MID) = TRIM(MD.MID)
    GROUP BY
        ACTOR_PID,
        DIRECTOR_PID
),
NUM_OF_MOVIES_BY_YC AS (
    SELECT
        NM.ACTOR_PID,
        NM.DIRECTOR_PID,
        NM.NUM_OF_MOV AS NUM_OF_MOV_BY_YC
    FROM
        NUM_OF_MOV_BY_ACTOR_DIRECTOR NM
    JOIN
        YASH_CHOPRAS_PID YCP ON NM.DIRECTOR_PID = YCP.PID
),
MAX_MOV_BY_OTHER_DIRECTORS AS (
    SELECT
        ACTOR_PID,
        MAX(NUM_OF_MOV) AS MAX_NUM_OF_MOV
    FROM
        NUM_OF_MOV_BY_ACTOR_DIRECTOR NM
    JOIN
        YASH_CHOPRAS_PID YCP ON NM.DIRECTOR_PID <> YCP.PID
    GROUP BY
        ACTOR_PID
),
ACTORS_MOV_COMPARISION AS (
    SELECT
        NMY.ACTOR_PID,
        CASE WHEN NMY.NUM_OF_MOV_BY_YC > IFNULL(NMO.MAX_NUM_OF_MOV, 0) THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS MORE_MOV_BY_YC
    FROM
        NUM_OF_MOVIES_BY_YC NMY
    LEFT OUTER JOIN
        MAX_MOV_BY_OTHER_DIRECTORS NMO ON NMY.ACTOR_PID = NMO.ACTOR_PID
)
SELECT
    COUNT(DISTINCT TRIM(P.PID)) AS "Number of actor"
FROM
    Person P
WHERE
    TRIM(P.PID) IN (
        SELECT
            DISTINCT ACTOR_PID
        FROM
            ACTORS_MOV_COMPARISION

question: Provide a detailed web sales report for each region, including the number of orders, total sales amount, and the name and sales amount of all sales representatives who achieved the highest total sales amount in that region (include all representatives in case of a tie).
generated_sql:
WITH region_summary AS (
    SELECT wr.id AS region_id,
           wr.name AS region_name,
           COUNT(o.id) AS order_count,
           SUM(o.total_amt_usd) AS region_total_sales
    FROM web_orders o
    JOIN web_accounts a ON o.account_id = a.id
    JOIN web_sales_reps rep ON a.sales_rep_id = rep.id
    JOIN web_region wr ON rep.region_id = wr.id
    GROUP BY wr.id, wr.name
), rep_sales AS (
    SELECT wr.id AS region_id,
           rep.name AS rep_name,
           SUM(o.total_amt_usd) AS rep_total_sales
    FROM web_orders o
    JOIN web_accounts a ON o.account_id = a.id
    JOIN web_sales_reps rep ON a.sales_rep_id = rep.id
    JOIN web_region wr ON rep.region_id = wr.id
    GROUP BY wr.id, rep.id, rep.name
), max_rep_sales AS (
    SELECT region_id,
           MAX(rep_total_sales) AS max_sales
    FROM rep_sales
    GROUP BY region_id
)
SELECT rs.region_name,
       rs.order_count,
       rs.region_total_sales,
       rp.rep_name,
       rp.rep_total_sales
FROM region_summary rs
JOIN rep_sales rp ON rs.region_id = rp.region_id
JOIN max_rep_sales mr ON rp.region_id = mr.region_id AND rp.rep_total_sales = mr.max_sales

question: Could you provide a list of last names for all students who have completed English courses (where completion is defined as having a ClassStatus of 2), along with their quintile ranks based on their individual grades in those courses? The quintile should be determined by calculating how many students have grades greater than or equal to each student's grade, then dividing this ranking by the total number of students who completed English courses. The quintiles should be labeled as "First" (top 20%), "Second" (top 21-40%), "Third" (top 41-60%), "Fourth" (top 61-80%), and "Fifth" (bottom 20%). Please sort the results from highest performing quintile to lowest (First to Fifth).
generated_sql:
WITH english_completed AS (
    SELECT s.StudLastName,
           ss.Grade
    FROM Student_Schedules ss
    JOIN Students s ON ss.StudentID = s.StudentID
    JOIN Classes c ON ss.ClassID = c.ClassID
    JOIN Subjects sub ON c.SubjectID = sub.SubjectID
    WHERE ss.ClassStatus = 2
      AND ss.Grade IS NOT NULL
      AND (LOWER(sub.SubjectName) LIKE '%english%' OR LOWER(sub.SubjectCode) LIKE '%eng%')
), ranked AS (
    SELECT StudLastName,
           Grade,
           COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY Grade DESC) AS rank_desc,
           COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_cnt
    FROM english_completed
)
SELECT StudLastName,
       CASE
           WHEN CAST(rank_desc AS REAL) / total_cnt <= 0.2 THEN 'First'
           WHEN CAST(rank_desc AS REAL) / total_cnt <= 0.4 THEN 'Second'
           WHEN CAST(rank_desc AS REAL) / total_cnt <= 0.6 THEN 'Third'
           WHEN CAST(rank_desc AS REAL) / total_cnt <= 0.8 THEN 'Fourth'
           ELSE 'Fifth'
       END AS Quintile
FROM ranked
ORDER BY CASE Quintile
            WHEN 'First' THEN 1
            WHEN 'Second' THEN 2
            WHEN 'Third' THEN 3
            WHEN 'Fourth' THEN 4
            ELSE 5
         END;

question: Given a database of musical styles and user preferences, where Musical_Preferences contains user rankings of musical styles (PreferenceSeq=1 for first choice, PreferenceSeq=2 for second choice, PreferenceSeq=3 for third choice): Calculate a weighted score for each musical style by assigning 3 points for each time it was ranked as first choice, 2 points for each second choice, and 1 point for each third choice ranking. Calculate the total weighted score for each musical style that has been ranked by at least one user. Then, compute the absolute difference between each style's total weighted score and the average total weighted score across all such styles.
generated_sql:
WITH style_scores AS (
    SELECT ms.StyleID,
           ms.StyleName,
           SUM(CASE mp.PreferenceSeq WHEN 1 THEN 3 WHEN 2 THEN 2 WHEN 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_score
    FROM Musical_Preferences mp
    JOIN Musical_Styles ms ON mp.StyleID = ms.StyleID
    GROUP BY ms.StyleID, ms.StyleName
    HAVING total_score > 0
), avg_score AS (
    SELECT AVG(total_score) AS avg_score FROM style_scores
)
SELECT ss.StyleName,
       ss.total_score,
       a.avg_score,
       ABS(ss.total_score - a.avg_score) AS diff
FROM style_scores ss
CROSS JOIN avg_score a
ORDER BY ss.StyleName;

question: How did each salesperson's annual total sales compare to their annual sales quota? Provide the difference between their total sales and the quota for each year, organized by salesperson and year.
generated_sql:
WITH sales_agg AS (
    SELECT soh.salespersonid,
           strftime('%Y', soh.orderdate) AS year,
           SUM(soh.totaldue) AS total_sales
    FROM salesorderheader soh
    WHERE soh.salespersonid IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY soh.salespersonid, strftime('%Y', soh.orderdate)
),
quota_agg AS (
    SELECT spqh.businessentityid,
           strftime('%Y', spqh.quotadate) AS year,
           SUM(spqh.salesquota) AS total_quota
    FROM SalesPersonQuotaHistory spqh
    GROUP BY spqh.businessentityid, strftime('%Y', spqh.quotadate)
)
SELECT COALESCE(s.salespersonid, q.businessentityid) AS salespersonid,
       COALESCE(s.year, q.year) AS year,
       COALESCE(s.total_sales, 0) - COALESCE(q.total_quota, 0) AS difference
FROM sales_agg s
FULL OUTER JOIN quota_agg q ON s.salespersonid = q.businessentityid AND s.year = q.year
ORDER BY salespersonid, year;

question: Can you provide the top 9 directors by movie count, including their ID, name, number of movies, average inter-movie duration (rounded to the nearest integer), average rating (rounded to 2 decimals), total votes, minimum and maximum ratings, and total movie duration? Sort the output first by movie count in descending order and then by total movie duration in descending order.
generated_sql:
WITH director_movies AS (
    SELECT dm.name_id AS director_id,
           n.name AS director_name,
           m.id AS movie_id,
           m.duration,
           m.date_published,
           r.avg_rating,
           r.total_votes
    FROM director_mapping dm
    JOIN movies m ON dm.movie_id = m.id
    JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
    LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
),
movie_gaps AS (
    SELECT director_id,
           director_name,
           movie_id,
           duration,
           avg_rating,
           total_votes,
           julianday(date_published) - julianday(LAG(date_published) OVER (PARTITION BY director_id ORDER BY date_published)) AS diff_days
    FROM director_movies
)
SELECT director_id,
       director_name,
       COUNT(movie_id) AS movie_count,
       ROUND(AVG(diff_days), 0) AS avg_inter_movie_duration,
       ROUND(AVG(avg_rating), 2) AS avg_rating,
       SUM(total_votes) AS total_votes,
       MIN(avg_rating) AS min_rating,
       MAX(avg_rating) AS max_rating,
       SUM(duration) AS total_duration
FROM movie_gaps
GROUP BY director_id, director_name
ORDER BY movie_count DESC, total_duration DESC
LIMIT 9;

question: Which university faculty members' salaries are closest to the average salary for their respective ranks? Please provide the ranks, first names, last names, and salaries.university
generated_sql:
WITH avg_salaries AS (
    SELECT FacRank, AVG(FacSalary) AS avg_salary
    FROM university_faculty
    GROUP BY FacRank
), diff_table AS (
    SELECT f.FacRank,
           f.FacFirstName,
           f.FacLastName,
           f.FacSalary,
           ABS(f.FacSalary - a.avg_salary) AS diff
    FROM university_faculty f
    JOIN avg_salaries a ON f.FacRank = a.FacRank
), min_diff AS (
    SELECT FacRank, MIN(diff) AS min_diff
    FROM diff_table
    GROUP BY FacRank
)
SELECT d.FacRank AS rank,
       d.FacFirstName AS first_name,
       d.FacLastName AS last_name,
       d.FacSalary AS salary
FROM diff_table d
JOIN min_diff m ON d.FacRank = m.FacRank AND d.diff = m.min_diff
ORDER BY d.FacRank;

WITH AvgSalaries AS (
    SELECT 
        facrank AS FacRank,
        AVG(facsalary) AS AvSalary
    FROM 
        university_faculty
    GROUP BY 
        facrank
),
SalaryDifferences AS (
    SELECT 
        university_faculty.facrank AS FacRank, 
        university_faculty.facfirstname AS FacFirstName, 
        university_faculty.faclastname AS FacLastName, 
        university_faculty.facsalary AS Salary, 
        ABS(university_faculty.facsalary - AvgSalaries.AvSalary) AS Diff
    FROM 
        university_faculty
    JOIN 
        AvgSalaries ON university_faculty.facrank = AvgSalaries.FacRank
),
MinDifferences AS (
    SELECT 
        FacRank, 
        MIN(Diff) AS MinDiff
    FROM 
        SalaryDifferences
    GROUP BY 
        FacRank
)
SELECT 
    s.FacRank, 
    s.FacFirstName, 
    s.FacLastName, 
    s.Salary
FROM 
    SalaryDifferences s
JOIN 
    MinDifferences m ON s.FacRank = m.FacRank AND s.Diff = m.MinDiff;

question: What is the annual retention rate of legislators who began their first term between January 1, 1917 and December 31, 1999, measured as the proportion of this cohort still in office on December 31st for each of the first 20 years following their initial term start? The results should show all 20 periods in sequence regardless of whether any legislators were retained in a particular year.
generated_sql:
WITH cohort AS (
    SELECT id_bioguide, MIN(date(term_start)) AS first_start
    FROM legislators_terms
    GROUP BY id_bioguide
    HAVING MIN(date(term_start)) >= '1917-01-01'
       AND MIN(date(term_start)) <= '1999-12-31'
),
total AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_cnt FROM cohort
),
years AS (
    SELECT 1 AS year_num
    UNION ALL
    SELECT year_num + 1 FROM years WHERE year_num < 20
),
retention AS (
    SELECT
        y.year_num,
        SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM legislators_terms lt
                WHERE lt.id_bioguide = c.id_bioguide
                  AND date(lt.term_start) <= date((CAST(strftime('%Y', c.first_start) AS INTEGER) + y.year_num - 1) || '-12-31')
                  AND (
                        lt.term_end IS NULL
                        OR lt.term_end = ''
                        OR date(lt.term_end) >= date((CAST(strftime('%Y', c.first_start) AS INTEGER) + y.year_num - 1) || '-12-31')
                      )
            ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retained_count
    FROM cohort c
    CROSS JOIN years y
    GROUP BY y.year_num
)
SELECT
    r.year_num,
    CASE WHEN t.total_cnt = 0 THEN 0 ELSE CAST(r.retained_count AS REAL) / t.total_cnt END AS retention_rate
FROM retention r
CROSS JOIN total t
ORDER BY r.year_num;

question: For male legislators from Louisiana, how many distinct legislators were actively serving on December 31 of each year from more than 30 years since their first term up to less than 50 years, grouping the results by the exact number of years elapsed since their first term?

WITH RECURSIVE first_terms AS (
    SELECT lt.id_bioguide,
           MIN(date(lt.term_start)) AS first_start
    FROM legislators_terms lt
    JOIN legislators l ON lt.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide
    WHERE (LOWER(l.gender) = 'male' OR LOWER(l.gender) = 'm')
      AND LOWER(lt.state) = 'la'
    GROUP BY lt.id_bioguide
), year_range AS (
    SELECT ft.id_bioguide,
           CAST(strftime('%Y', ft.first_start) AS INTEGER) + 31 AS year,
           31 AS years_elapsed
    FROM first_terms ft
    UNION ALL
    SELECT yr.id_bioguide,
           yr.year + 1,
           yr.years_elapsed + 1
    FROM year_range yr
    WHERE yr.years_elapsed < 49
)

FROM year_range yr

    FROM legislators_terms lt
    WHERE lt.id_bioguide = yr.id_bioguide
      AND date(yr.year || '-12-31') >= date(lt.term_start)
      AND (lt.term_end IS NULL OR date(yr.year || '-12-31') <= date(lt.term_end))
)

question: Could you find out the average percentage of the total lifetime sales (LTV) that occur in the first 7 and 30 days after a customer's initial purchase? Also, include the average total lifetime sales (LTV). Please exclude customers with zero lifetime sales. The 7- and 30-day periods should be based on the exact number of hours-minutes-seconds, not calendar days.
generated_sql:
WITH first_payment AS (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(payment_date) AS first_date
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_sales AS (
    SELECT p.customer_id,
           SUM(p.amount) AS total_ltv,
           SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_date <= datetime(fp.first_date, '+7 days') THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_7d,
           SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_date <= datetime(fp.first_date, '+30 days') THEN p.amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_30d
    FROM payment p
    JOIN first_payment fp ON p.customer_id = fp.customer_id
    GROUP BY p.customer_id
    HAVING total_ltv > 0
)
SELECT AVG(CAST(sum_7d AS REAL) / total_ltv * 100.0) AS avg_7day_pct,
       AVG(CAST(sum_30d AS REAL) / total_ltv * 100.0) AS avg_30day_pct,
       AVG(total_ltv) AS avg_ltv
FROM customer_sales;

question: Please provide a list of the top three revenue-generating films for each actor, along with the average revenue per actor in those films, calculated by dividing the total film revenue equally among the actors for each film.
generated_sql:
WITH film_revenue AS (
    SELECT f.film_id,
           f.title,
           SUM(p.amount) AS total_revenue
    FROM film f
    JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
    JOIN rental r ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    JOIN payment p ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
    GROUP BY f.film_id
),
film_actor_counts AS (
    SELECT film_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT actor_id) AS actor_count
    FROM film_actor
    GROUP BY film_id
),
film_stats AS (
    SELECT fr.film_id,
           fr.title,
           fr.total_revenue,
           fac.actor_count,
           fr.total_revenue / CAST(fac.actor_count AS REAL) AS revenue_share
    FROM film_revenue fr
    JOIN film_actor_counts fac ON fac.film_id = fr.film_id
),
actor_film AS (
    SELECT a.actor_id,
           a.first_name,
           a.last_name,
           fs.title,
           fs.total_revenue,
           fs.revenue_share
    FROM actor a
    JOIN film_actor fa ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
    JOIN film_stats fs ON fs.film_id = fa.film_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY actor_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC) AS rn
    FROM actor_film
)
SELECT first_name,
       last_name,
       title,
       AVG(revenue_share) OVER (PARTITION BY actor_id) AS average_revenue_per_actor
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY first_name, last_name, rn;

question: For each rating category of the first movie rented by customers—where the first movie is identified based on the earliest payment date per customer—please provide the average total amount spent per customer and the average number of subsequent rentals (calculated as the total number of rentals minus one) for customers whose first rented movie falls into that rating category.
generated_sql:
WITH first_movie AS (
  SELECT p.customer_id, f.rating
  FROM (
    SELECT payment_id, customer_id, rental_id, payment_date,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY payment_date) AS rn
    FROM payment
  ) p
  JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  WHERE p.rn = 1
),
payment_agg AS (
  SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spent
  FROM payment
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
rental_agg AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(rental_id) AS total_rentals
  FROM rental
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
combined AS (
  SELECT fm.rating,
         pa.total_spent,
         COALESCE(ra.total_rentals, 0) - 1 AS subsequent_rentals
  FROM first_movie fm
  JOIN payment_agg pa ON fm.customer_id = pa.customer_id
  LEFT JOIN rental_agg ra ON fm.customer_id = ra.customer_id
)
SELECT rating,
       AVG(total_spent) AS avg_total_spent,
       AVG(subsequent_rentals) AS avg_subsequent_rentals
FROM combined
GROUP BY rating
ORDER BY rating;

question: Among our top 10 paying customers, can you identify the largest change in payment amounts from one month to the immediately following month? Specifically, please determine for which customer and during which month this maximum month-over-month difference occurred, and provide the difference rounded to two decimal places.
generated_sql:
WITH top_customers AS (
    SELECT customer_id
    FROM payment
    GROUP BY customer_id
    ORDER BY SUM(amount) DESC
    LIMIT 10
),
monthly AS (
    SELECT p.customer_id,
           strftime('%Y-%m', p.payment_date) AS month,
           SUM(p.amount) AS month_total
    FROM payment p
    JOIN top_customers tc ON p.customer_id = tc.customer_id
    GROUP BY p.customer_id, month
),
monthly_diff AS (
    SELECT m.customer_id,
           m.month,
           m.month_total,
           LAG(m.month_total) OVER (PARTITION BY m.customer_id ORDER BY m.month) AS prev_total,
           ROUND(ABS(m.month_total - LAG(m.month_total) OVER (PARTITION BY m.customer_id ORDER BY m.month)), 2) AS diff
    FROM monthly m
)
SELECT c.first_name,
       c.last_name,
       d.month,
       d.diff
FROM monthly_diff d
JOIN customer c ON d.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE d.prev_total IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY d.diff DESC
LIMIT 1;

  SELECT 
    strftime('%m', pm.payment_date) AS pay_mon, 
    customer_id,
    COUNT(pm.amount) AS pay_countpermon, 
    SUM(pm.amount) AS pay_amount 
  FROM 
    payment AS pm 
  GROUP BY 
    pay_mon, 
    customer_id
), 
top10_customer AS (
  SELECT 
    customer_id,
    SUM(tb.pay_amount) AS total_payments 
  FROM 
    result_table AS tb 
  GROUP BY 
    customer_id
  ORDER BY 
    SUM(tb.pay_amount) DESC 
  LIMIT 
    10
), 
difference_per_mon AS (
  SELECT 
    pay_mon AS month_number, 
    pay_mon AS month, 
    tb.pay_countpermon, 
    tb.pay_amount, 
    ABS(tb.pay_amount - LAG(tb.pay_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY tb.customer_id)) AS diff 
  FROM 
    result_table tb 
    JOIN top10_customer top ON top.customer_id = tb.customer_id
) 
SELECT 
  month, 
  ROUND(max_diff, 2) AS max_diff 
FROM (
  SELECT 
    month, 
    diff, 
    month_number, 
    MAX(diff) OVER (PARTITION BY month) AS max_diff 
  FROM 
    difference_per_mon

WHERE 
  diff = max_diff 
ORDER BY 
  max_diff DESC

question: Using the sales data, what is the median value of total sales made in countries where the number of customers is greater than 4?
generated_sql:
WITH country_sales AS (
  SELECT c.Country,
         COUNT(DISTINCT c.CustomerId) AS cust_count,
         COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total_sales
  FROM customers c
  LEFT JOIN invoices i ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
  GROUP BY c.Country
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.CustomerId) > 4
)
SELECT AVG(total_sales) AS median_total_sales
FROM (
  SELECT total_sales,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM country_sales
) sub
WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2);

question: Can you identify the year and month with the highest rental orders created by the store's staff for each store? Please list the store ID, the year, the month, and the total rentals for those dates.
generated_sql:
WITH rental_counts AS (
    SELECT s.store_id,
           strftime('%Y', r.rental_date) AS year,
           strftime('%m', r.rental_date) AS month,
           COUNT(*) AS total_rentals
    FROM rental r
    JOIN staff s ON r.staff_id = s.staff_id
    GROUP BY s.store_id, year, month
), max_counts AS (
    SELECT store_id,
           MAX(total_rentals) AS max_rentals
    FROM rental_counts
    GROUP BY store_id
)
SELECT rc.store_id,
       rc.year,
       rc.month,
       rc.total_rentals
FROM rental_counts rc
JOIN max_counts mc ON rc.store_id = mc.store_id AND rc.total_rentals = mc.max_rentals;

  SELECT 
    strftime('%Y', RE.RENTAL_DATE) AS YEAR, 
    strftime('%m', RE.RENTAL_DATE) AS RENTAL_MONTH,

    COUNT(RE.RENTAL_ID) AS count 
  FROM

question: For alien data, how many of the top 10 states by alien population have a higher percentage of friendly aliens than hostile aliens, with an average alien age exceeding 200?
generated_sql:

FROM (
    SELECT state,
           COUNT(*) AS total_count,
           SUM(CASE WHEN aggressive = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS friendly_count,
           SUM(CASE WHEN aggressive = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS hostile_count,
           AVG(age) AS avg_age
    FROM alien_data
    GROUP BY state
    ORDER BY total_count DESC
    LIMIT 10
) AS top10

question: Can you identify the hubs that saw more than a 20% increase in finished orders from February to March?
generated_sql:
WITH feb AS (
    SELECT h.hub_id, h.hub_name, COUNT(*) AS feb_cnt
    FROM orders o
    JOIN stores s ON o.store_id = s.store_id
    JOIN hubs h ON s.hub_id = h.hub_id
    WHERE LOWER(o.order_status) = 'finished'
      AND o.order_created_month = 2
    GROUP BY h.hub_id, h.hub_name
), mar AS (
    SELECT h.hub_id, COUNT(*) AS mar_cnt
    FROM orders o
    JOIN stores s ON o.store_id = s.store_id
    JOIN hubs h ON s.hub_id = h.hub_id
    WHERE LOWER(o.order_status) = 'finished'
      AND o.order_created_month = 3
    GROUP BY h.hub_id
)
SELECT f.hub_name
FROM feb f
JOIN mar m ON f.hub_id = m.hub_id
WHERE f.feb_cnt > 0
  AND (CAST(m.mar_cnt AS REAL) - f.feb_cnt) / f.feb_cnt > 0.20;

    SELECT
        h.hub_name AS hub_name,
        COUNT(*) AS orders_february
    FROM 
        orders o 
    LEFT JOIN
        stores s ON o.store_id = s.store_id 
    LEFT JOIN 
        hubs h ON s.hub_id = h.hub_id 
    WHERE o.order_created_month = 2 AND o.order_status = 'FINISHED'
    GROUP BY
        h.hub_name
),
march_orders AS (
    SELECT
        h.hub_name AS hub_name,
        COUNT(*) AS orders_march
    FROM 
        orders o 
    LEFT JOIN
        stores s ON o.store_id = s.store_id 
    LEFT JOIN 
        hubs h ON s.hub_id = h.hub_id 
    WHERE o.order_created_month = 3 AND o.order_status = 'FINISHED'
    GROUP BY
        h.hub_name
)
SELECT
    fo.hub_name
FROM
    february_orders fo
LEFT JOIN 
    march_orders mo ON fo.hub_name = mo.hub_name
WHERE 
    fo.orders_february > 0 AND 
    mo.orders_march > 0 AND
    (CAST((mo.orders_march - fo.orders_february) AS REAL) / CAST(fo.orders_february AS REAL)) > 0.2  -- Filter for hubs with more than a 20% increase

question: Can you calculate the median from the highest season goals of each team?
generated_sql:
WITH team_season_goals AS (
  SELECT home_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
         season,
         SUM(home_team_goal) AS goals
  FROM Match
  GROUP BY home_team_api_id, season
  UNION ALL
  SELECT away_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
         season,
         SUM(away_team_goal) AS goals
  FROM Match
  GROUP BY away_team_api_id, season
), team_total_goals AS (
  SELECT team_api_id,
         season,
         SUM(goals) AS total_goals
  FROM team_season_goals
  GROUP BY team_api_id, season
), team_max_goals AS (
  SELECT team_api_id,
         MAX(total_goals) AS max_goals
  FROM team_total_goals
  GROUP BY team_api_id
), ranked AS (
  SELECT max_goals,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY max_goals) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM team_max_goals
)
SELECT AVG(max_goals) AS median
FROM ranked
WHERE (cnt % 2 = 1 AND rn = (cnt + 1) / 2)
   OR (cnt % 2 = 0 AND (rn = cnt / 2 OR rn = cnt / 2 + 1));

question: Find the IDs of players who scored the highest number of partnership runs for each match. The output should include the IDs of two players, each with their individual scores and the total partnership score. For each pair, the player with the higher individual score should be listed as player 1, and the player with the lower score as player 2. In cases where both players have the same score, the player with the higher ID should be player 1, and the player with the lower ID should be player 2. There can be multiple rows for a single match.
generated_sql:
WITH partnership_raw AS (
    SELECT 
        b.match_id,
        CASE WHEN b.striker < b.non_striker THEN b.striker ELSE b.non_striker END AS p_a,
        CASE WHEN b.striker < b.non_striker THEN b.non_striker ELSE b.striker END AS p_b,
        b.striker AS striker_id,
        bs.runs_scored
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    JOIN batsman_scored bs ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
        AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
        AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
        AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
), partnership_agg AS (
    SELECT 
        match_id,
        p_a,
        p_b,
        SUM(runs_scored) AS partnership_total,
        SUM(CASE WHEN striker_id = p_a THEN runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS p_a_score,
        SUM(CASE WHEN striker_id = p_b THEN runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS p_b_score
    FROM partnership_raw
    GROUP BY match_id, p_a, p_b
), max_total AS (
    SELECT match_id, MAX(partnership_total) AS max_total
    FROM partnership_agg
    GROUP BY match_id
)
SELECT 
    pa.match_id,
    CASE 
        WHEN pa.p_a_score > pa.p_b_score THEN pa.p_a
        WHEN pa.p_b_score > pa.p_a_score THEN pa.p_b
        ELSE CASE WHEN pa.p_a > pa.p_b THEN pa.p_a ELSE pa.p_b END
    END AS player1_id,
    CASE 
        WHEN pa.p_a_score > pa.p_b_score THEN pa.p_a_score
        WHEN pa.p_b_score > pa.p_a_score THEN pa.p_b_score
        ELSE CASE WHEN pa.p_a > pa.p_b THEN pa.p_a_score ELSE pa.p_b_score END
    END AS player1_score,
    CASE 
        WHEN pa.p_a_score > pa.p_b_score THEN pa.p_b
        WHEN pa.p_b_score > pa.p_a_score THEN pa.p_a
        ELSE CASE WHEN pa.p_a > pa.p_b THEN pa.p_b ELSE pa.p_a END
    END AS player2_id,
    CASE 
        WHEN pa.p_a_score > pa.p_b_score THEN pa.p_b_score
        WHEN pa.p_b_score > pa.p_a_score THEN pa.p_a_score
        ELSE CASE WHEN pa.p_a > pa.p_b THEN pa.p_b_score ELSE pa.p_a_score END
    END AS player2_score,
    pa.partnership_total
FROM partnership_agg pa
JOIN max_total mt ON pa.match_id = mt.match_id AND pa.partnership_total = mt.max_total;

question: Determine the top three genres with the most movies rated above 8, and then identify the top four directors who have directed the most films rated above 8 within those genres. List these directors and their respective movie counts.

question: Calculate the duration of each track, classify them as short, medium, or long, output the minimum and maximum time for each kind (in minutes) and the total revenue for each category, group by the category.

SELECT category,
       MIN(duration_min) AS min_duration,
       MAX(duration_min) AS max_duration,
       SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue
FROM (
    SELECT CASE
               WHEN CAST(t.Milliseconds AS REAL) / 60000 < 3 THEN 'short'
               WHEN CAST(t.Milliseconds AS REAL) / 60000 <= 5 THEN 'medium'
               ELSE 'long'
           END AS category,
           CAST(t.Milliseconds AS REAL) / 60000 AS duration_min,
           COALESCE(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 0) AS revenue
    FROM Track t
    LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
    GROUP BY t.TrackId
) sub

question: Using a Salary Dataset where the salary values need to be cleaned by removing non-numeric characters and converting them to a numeric type, write a detailed SQL query that identifies the top 5 companies by average salary in each of Mumbai, Pune, New Delhi, and Hyderabad, then compares each company’s average salary in those cities to the overall national average salary. The final result should display four columns: Location, Company Name, Average Salary in State, and Average Salary in Country, listing only the top 5 companies in each of the specified locations.
generated_sql:
WITH cleaned AS (
    SELECT 
        CompanyName,
        LOWER(Location) AS location,
        CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(Salary, '$', ''), ',', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL) AS clean_salary
    FROM SalaryDataset
    WHERE LOWER(Location) IN ('mumbai', 'pune', 'new delhi', 'hyderabad')
      AND Salary IS NOT NULL
      AND TRIM(Salary) <> ''
),
valid_clean AS (
    SELECT CompanyName,
           location,
           clean_salary
    FROM cleaned
    WHERE clean_salary IS NOT NULL
),
national_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(clean_salary) AS avg_salary_country
    FROM valid_clean
),
loc_company_avg AS (
    SELECT location,
           CompanyName,
           AVG(clean_salary) AS avg_salary_state
    FROM valid_clean
    GROUP BY location, CompanyName
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT lca.location,
           lca.CompanyName,
           lca.avg_salary_state,
           na.avg_salary_country,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lca.location ORDER BY lca.avg_salary_state DESC) AS rn
    FROM loc_company_avg lca
    CROSS JOIN national_avg na
)
SELECT 
    location AS Location,
    CompanyName AS "Company Name",
    COALESCE(avg_salary_state, 0) AS "Average Salary in State",
    COALESCE(avg_salary_country, 0) AS "Average Salary in Country"
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 5
ORDER BY location, avg_salary_state DESC;

question: Identify the L1_model associated with each model (specified by name and version) that occurs most frequently for each status ('strong' or 'soft'), along with the number of times it occurs. A model has a 'strong' status if, for any of its steps, the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models is less than the 'Stack' model's test score. It has a 'soft' status if the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models equals the 'Stack' model's test score. Count how many times each L1_model is associated with a 'strong' or 'soft' status across all models, and determine which L1_model has the highest occurrence for each status.
generated_sql:
WITH model_max AS (
    SELECT name,
           version,
           MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER(model) = LOWER('stack') THEN test_score END) AS stack_max_score,
           MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER(model) != LOWER('stack') THEN test_score END) AS nonstack_max_score
    FROM model_score
    GROUP BY name, version
),
model_status AS (
    SELECT name,
           version,
           CASE
               WHEN stack_max_score > nonstack_max_score THEN 'strong'
               WHEN stack_max_score = nonstack_max_score THEN 'soft'
           END AS status
    FROM model_max
    WHERE stack_max_score IS NOT NULL AND nonstack_max_score IS NOT NULL
),
model_l1 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT name,
                    version,
                    L1_model
    FROM model
),
final_counts AS (
    SELECT l1.L1_model,
           ms.status,
           COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM model_status ms
    JOIN model_l1 l1 ON ms.name = l1.name AND ms.version = l1.version
    WHERE ms.status IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY l1.L1_model, ms.status
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT L1_model,
           status,
           cnt,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY status ORDER BY cnt DESC) AS rn
    FROM final_counts
)
SELECT L1_model,
       status,
       cnt
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1;

question: What is the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations, considering only the leaf-level items within each combination after fully expanding any nested packaging relationships?

WITH RECURSIVE expanded(root_id, leaf_id, qty) AS (
    SELECT pr.packaging_id, pr.contains_id, pr.qty
    FROM packaging_relations pr
    UNION ALL
    SELECT e.root_id, pr.contains_id, e.qty * pr.qty
    FROM expanded e
    JOIN packaging_relations pr ON e.leaf_id = pr.packaging_id
),
leaf_totals AS (
    SELECT root_id, SUM(qty) AS total_qty
    FROM expanded
    WHERE leaf_id NOT IN (SELECT packaging_id FROM packaging_relations)
    GROUP BY root_id
),
root_packages AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT packaging_id AS root_id
    FROM packaging_relations
    WHERE packaging_id NOT IN (SELECT contains_id FROM packaging_relations)

question: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.
generated_sql:
WITH order_lines AS (
    SELECT ol.id AS line_id,
           ol.product_id,
           ol.qty,
           SUM(ol.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY ol.id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS cum_req_qty,
           SUM(ol.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY ol.id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) - ol.qty AS prev_cum_req_qty
    FROM orderlines ol
    WHERE ol.order_id = 423
),
inv AS (
    SELECT i.product_id,
           i.location_id,
           i.qty AS inv_qty,
           l.aisle,
           l.position,
           p.purchased
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
),
inv_sorted AS (
    SELECT inv.*, 
           SUM(inv.inv_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY inv.product_id ORDER BY inv.purchased ASC, inv.inv_qty ASC ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS cum_inv_qty
    FROM inv
),
alloc AS (
    SELECT ol.line_id,
           inv.product_id,
           inv.aisle,
           inv.position,
           (
               CASE
                   WHEN inv.cum_inv_qty <= ol.cum_req_qty THEN inv.inv_qty
                   WHEN inv.cum_inv_qty - inv.inv_qty < ol.cum_req_qty THEN ol.cum_req_qty - (inv.cum_inv_qty - inv.inv_qty)
                   ELSE 0
               END
           ) - (
               CASE
                   WHEN inv.cum_inv_qty <= ol.prev_cum_req_qty THEN inv.inv_qty
                   WHEN inv.cum_inv_qty - inv.inv_qty < ol.prev_cum_req_qty THEN ol.prev_cum_req_qty - (inv.cum_inv_qty - inv.inv_qty)
                   ELSE 0
               END
           ) AS pick_qty
    FROM inv_sorted inv
    JOIN order_lines ol ON inv.product_id = ol.product_id
    WHERE (
              CASE
                  WHEN inv.cum_inv_qty <= ol.cum_req_qty THEN inv.inv_qty
                  WHEN inv.cum_inv_qty - inv.inv_qty < ol.cum_req_qty THEN ol.cum_req_qty - (inv.cum_inv_qty - inv.inv_qty)
                  ELSE 0
              END
          ) - (
              CASE
                  WHEN inv.cum_inv_qty <= ol.prev_cum_req_qty THEN inv.inv_qty
                  WHEN inv.cum_inv_qty - inv.inv_qty < ol.prev_cum_req_qty THEN ol.prev_cum_req_qty - (inv.cum_inv_qty - inv.inv_qty)
                  ELSE 0
              END
          ) > 0
)
SELECT line_id, product_id, aisle, position, pick_qty
FROM alloc
ORDER BY product_id, line_id, aisle, position;

question: Calculate the average pick percentage for each product name, using a first-in-first-out approach that selects from inventory locations based on the earliest purchase date and smallest available quantity, ensuring that the picked quantity reflects only the overlapping range between each order’s required quantity and the inventory’s available quantity, and then grouping and ordering the results by product name?
generated_sql:
WITH inv_fifo AS (
    SELECT i.id AS inv_id,
           i.product_id,
           i.qty,
           p.purchased AS purchase_date,
           SUM(i.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty, i.id) AS cum_inv_qty,
           SUM(i.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty, i.id) - i.qty + 1 AS inv_start
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
),
orders_fifo AS (
    SELECT ol.id AS ol_id,
           ol.product_id,
           ol.qty AS order_qty,
           o.ordered AS order_date,
           SUM(ol.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY o.ordered, ol.id) AS cum_order_qty,
           SUM(ol.qty) OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY o.ordered, ol.id) - ol.qty + 1 AS order_start
    FROM orderlines ol
    JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.id
),
alloc AS (
    SELECT o.ol_id,
           o.product_id,
           o.order_qty,
           SUM(
               CASE
                   WHEN o.order_start <= i.cum_inv_qty AND o.cum_order_qty >= i.inv_start
                   THEN MIN(o.cum_order_qty, i.cum_inv_qty) - MAX(o.order_start, i.inv_start) + 1
                   ELSE 0
               END
           ) AS allocated_qty
    FROM orders_fifo o
    JOIN inv_fifo i
      ON o.product_id = i.product_id
     AND o.order_start <= i.cum_inv_qty
     AND o.cum_order_qty >= i.inv_start
    GROUP BY o.ol_id, o.product_id, o.order_qty
),
pick AS (
    SELECT a.product_id,
           CAST(a.allocated_qty AS REAL) / a.order_qty AS pick_pct
    FROM alloc a
)
SELECT p.name AS product_name,
       AVG(pick_pct) AS avg_pick_percentage
FROM pick
JOIN products p ON pick.product_id = p.id
GROUP BY p.name
ORDER BY p.name;
